reviewed_by: Claude review of the vendor-native capability containment boundary
reason: Harness sessions freeze an execution mode next to their native capabilities, and 08be66f dropped the container-only clamp from _session_native_capabilities, so adapters trusted whatever capability flags session metadata carried: tests/v3/test_harness_adapters.py::test_claude_native_capabilities_exclude_project_files_and_shell has been failing on main with Read/Glob/Grep/Bash leaking into a contained session. _session_native_capabilities now clamps (never grants) back to container-only unless the session froze execution_mode 'host'. Selected both files that own this policy in full: test_harness_adapters.py covers each vendor's config boundary (Claude tool set, disallowed_tools, PreToolUse decisions and system prompt on both sides of the clamp, and the Grok --disallowed-tools argv with its host fixture now carrying the execution_mode the runtime persists), and test_harnesses.py covers the runtime service that freezes capabilities per execution mode, forks sessions when a project changes mode, backfills legacy sessions, and denies legacy host shell flags.
exclusions: No full suites. The change is confined to one backend policy helper plus the single reader of session capability metadata, so no UI file, style, API schema, or native module changed: frontend, native and Playwright layers are not applicable. Other Python files are excluded because they neither read native capabilities nor construct harness sessions; tests/v3/test_harness_commands.py, test_harness_connection_state.py, test_approval_handoff.py, test_browser_companion.py and test_diagnostic_guidance.py were run locally against this diff (82 passed) and are excluded as unaffected; rebased onto #368/#371/#373 and both selected files re-run green. Live provider turns and real-Core host-mode journeys are excluded; the host execution path is exercised through the runtime service fixtures.
